quest.title: Opening Festivities
quest.description: Paimon heard from someone or somewhere news about the Akademiya Extravaganza. Head to the Akademiya and ask around for details.
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6, Tahchin x2

chapter.num: A Parade of Providence: Act I
chapter.title: Comings and Goings

talks.objective: Head to the Akademiya's Main Hall to ask around for news

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: #A moment, if you would... Are you two the famous {NICKNAME} and Paimon, by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We sure are! And who're you?

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: My name is Wiqas, a member of the Akademiya Extravaganza Planning Committee. Have you two heard of this festival?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Only just now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup, and that's exactly why we're here!

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: Is that so? Looks like our advertising is working.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: Since you're both interested, would you mind if I gave you a brief explanation of the event?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That would be helpful, thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: Ahem... So, the Akademiya Extravaganza is a grand event run by the Akademiya with a long and storied history. To be precise, it can be divided into the Wisdom Gala and the Interdarshan Championship.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: The Gala is held annually. During this time, all six Darshans will set up booths throughout the city and host guests to showcase the most fascinating aspects of their school and thus increase their influence.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: On the other hand, the Championship is held once every four years. Each Darshan will send a representative to vie for the position of grand champion.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: This year, the Gala is being held alongside the Championship, so the mood in the city is, as they say, at an unprecedented fever pitch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Got it! Cool, thanks a bunch for the detailed explanation!

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: You're most welcome. Answering questions regarding the Akademiya Extravaganza is my job, and... I actually do have something I would like to ask the two of you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Need our help with something?

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: Well... Let me begin by saying that this year's Akademiya Extravaganza is of utmost importance to us.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: Lesser Lord Kusanali and the sages came up with a plan for the Akademiya to recruit talented people from the desert, starting next year.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: As such, we've invited a great number of desert-dwellers to take part in this festival, so they can hopefully experience the Akademiya's atmosphere ahead of time.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: I've heard that the two of you are famous across both the rainforest and desert. With your participation, especially in the Interdarshan Championship, more people will definitely come to appreciate the festival.

choices.text: We're not Akademiya researchers, you know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly. Or do you mean you want us to join a Darshan? Ugh, but then we'd have to deal with exams and essays and stuff like that...

response.speaker: Wiqas
response.text: No need to worry. The Championship participants have already been selected. I mean to invite the two of you as guest commentators. Your job will be to observe and record every part of the competition.

response.speaker: Wiqas
response.text: There's no pressure. Just follow each match and enjoy the festival! Aside from that, we'll also prepare some compensation for your efforts — we won't have you working for free.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That kinda sounds like a sweet deal. What do you think?

response.speaker: Wiqas
response.text: You can head over to the festival venue later. An organizer there will introduce each participant.

response.speaker: Wiqas
response.text: Some of them even might be people you recognize... I'll leave it at that for now.

response.speaker: Wiqas
response.text: So, how about it? Would you like to take this commission?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll give it a go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, having fun while getting paid... This sounds awesome!

response.speaker: Wiqas
response.text: The main event venue is at the outskirts of the Citadel of Regzar, and the organizer you're looking for is Kareena. Tell her the situation and she'll get you set up.

response.speaker: Wiqas
response.text: The Championship is going to begin soon. I wish you a good experience serving as commentators. If you have any doubts, come find me any time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alrighty, off we go!

response.speaker: Wiqas
response.text: Yes. Two others, in fact.

response.speaker: Wiqas
response.text: Their responsibilities will be somewhat different from yours. One of our organizers will explain the details to you later at the main venue.

choices.text: Didn't you just say that only Darshan representatives can take part?

talks.objective: Head to the Akademiya Extravaganza's main venue

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Welcome, one and all, to the Akademiya Extravaganza!

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Now then, allow me to reveal the prizes for this iteration of the Interdarshan Championship—

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Fabulous monetary rewards, research funds, a limited-edition Genius Invokation TCG card... and the right to wear the Diadem of Knowledge. I believe that I need not elaborate as to how this is a symbol of great honor!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She should be Kareena, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like she's in the middle of something. Let's wait till she's less busy, then go introduce ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Alae
dialogues.text: The Diadem of Knowledge... What a perfect work of art...

dialogues.speaker: Aissa
dialogues.text: Every time I see it, I feel like I'm losing myself in its beauty. The one who proves fit to wear it must be a rare genius indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: I believe that most of you have already seen the Diadem of Knowledge, or have heard tales about it.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Twenty years ago, a researcher named Sachin bought it for a large sum of Mora before donating it to the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: The generous Championship prizes are also sourced from his sponsorship. Before we begin, allow me to express our gratitude to this researcher, who cannot be with us right now...
Things can only get worse...
Things can only go from bad... to worse...

response.text: Human nature begets conflict, and conflict begets ruin. From the beginning, the seeds of wickedness have been...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, stop spacing out!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon called out to you, but you didn't respond. You okay? Did you stay up late without telling Paimon?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I was...

response.speaker: Kareena
response.text: Alright, I'm sure we're all more than ready for the Championship to begin!

response.speaker: Kareena
response.text: Now then, let's invite our six Darshan representatives to the stage! Our contestants are—

response.speaker: Kareena
response.text: Representing Amurta, Tighnari!

response.speaker: Kareena
response.text: Representing Spantamad, Cyno!

response.speaker: Kareena
response.text: Representing Rtawahist, Layla!

response.speaker: Kareena
response.text: Representing Haravatat, Faruzan!

response.speaker: Kareena
response.text: Representing Kshahrewar, Kaveh!

response.speaker: Kareena
response.text: And for Vahumana... Huh? Is Vahumana's representative not here yet?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: These introductions are pointless. Let's just get this over with.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? W—Wait a sec, why is he Vahumana's representative...?

response.speaker: Kareena
response.text: Finally! Our final contestant is Vahumana's representative: Hat Guy!

response.speaker: Alae
response.text: Oh, so that's Hat Guy? I think I've seen him before...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? You know who he is?

response.speaker: Aissa
response.text: I've heard that he's a researcher from a different country who nominally belongs to Vahumana. Word is that he's written a lot of political analyses.

response.speaker: Aissa
response.text: His manner of speech hasn't made him popular amongst most other Vahumana researchers, but his comings and goings are quite irregular, so he doesn't interact with others much.

response.speaker: Alae
response.text: Aside from his more controversial aspects, his perspectives are considered quite incisive.

response.speaker: Alae
response.text: Vahumana has seen a dearth of new talent lately, and some of its existing ones are not currently at the Akademiya, so I suspect he might have been their only option...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's just kinda weird. He doesn't seem like the kind of guy who'd participate in competitions like this one...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm quite puzzled, too.

response.speaker: Kareena
response.text: Now that we have our six contestants, the Championship will soon begin!

response.speaker: Kareena
response.text: Who will triumph this time around? Hold on to your hats, because we're all on this ride together!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, we really do know a lot of the contestants.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, right, we're guest commentators, aren't we? So figuring out everyone's reasons for participating is in our job description.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go ask them when we go say hi. Especially him... Paimon still thinks it's weird that he's here.

talks.objective: Ask the representatives their reasons for participation

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: We meet again, you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Tighnari! We came here to check out this Extravaganza event... and then they invited us to be guest commentators!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Is that so? I heard that there would be guest commentators recording the proceedings with Kameras, but I didn't expect they'd be you two.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It's a pleasant surprise that you're visiting Sumeru again while I'm still on leave. When everything comes together perfectly like this, I call it the Biryani factor:

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Because it's always rice to meat stew again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sooo, Tighnari, you're representing Amurta, and Cyno is representing Spantamad...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But haven't you both already graduated? Can alumni also take part in the competition?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I had wondered the same thing. When I was told the news, I was actually more shocked than you are now.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I later found out that anyone who has been part of a particular Darshan has the right to participate. Graduation status has no effect.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's a rule, huh.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: There are some restrictions, though. For example, sages cannot participate, any given person can only participate in one instance of the Championship, and so on.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That's right. Also, there are two methods by which the Darshan representatives are chosen. One is self-nomination, and the other is to be recommended by over half of one's Darshan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You must've been a case of the latter, Tighnari!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I heard that quite a few of your juniors petitioned for your candidacy.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...Sometimes I wish I could clap a few of them over the head and tell them to spend that time on studying instead.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can you refuse?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, you can. But after some consideration, I realized this could be a good opportunity for me.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Next month, we're having a public lecture on ecology at Gandharva Ville. If I participate in this event, I might be able to utilize its popularity to promote the lecture.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'm not that concerned about becoming the champion, unlike someone here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you volunteered yourself, Cyno?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yes. I'm using the last of my leave for this. When I heard that a limited-edition Genius Invokation TCG card was one of the prizes, I signed myself up.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: This year's card is a rare one indeed. It would be a shame if I missed out on it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... Is it some kind of super powerful card?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: No, it's a very common one, but it has a holographic layer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? So what's the point?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It's very cool.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Paimon meant apart from being "very cool."

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That is reason enough. I shall do my all to emerge victorious and add it to my deck.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: As someone who doesn't play cards much, I can't quite relate... but it isn't surprising that everyone has their own reasons for taking part in the tournament.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fair enough. Alright, let's go find someone else to question.

talks.objective: Ask the representatives their reasons for participation

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kaveh, Faruzan, Layla!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh, it's you. Why're you here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're here as specially invited guest commentators! Our job is to record what happens during the competition!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Is that so? In that case, I'll have to trouble you to catch the moment of my triumph on Kamera!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Remember to shoot from behind at a lower angle — you know, to capture a senior's class!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Don't get ahead of yourself, now. Victory will obviously be mine!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Hah, you're far too young to even consider challenging me. Kshahrewar or Rtawahist, you're all children as far as I'm concerned...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: A—Actually, I was going to ask... How do you know me, Madam Faruzan?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Hmm? You don't remember? I sometimes see you in the library at night. You even waved at me!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: What...? I don't remember doing that at all!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: How strange... However, this is not the time for curiosity. I am Faruzan, a household name in Haravatat. You are Layla from Rtawahist, I presume?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Y—Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Good, then we are officially introduced. See? Simple as that.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I like respectful ones, by the way. Would you like to join my research group?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Madam Faruzan... I'm quite sure this counts as poaching. Let's dial things down...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I know, but it's been tough getting people these days, and research funding has been hard to secure...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: But once I win this tournament, it'll be a different story...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you're just here to increase the amount of funding you're getting?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Well, not just that... What, are you curious about my reasons for participating in this event?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Well, I suppose that's to be expected. You are our guest commentators, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: There's been an influx of newly enrolled students, and they'll be paying close attention to this competition. If I do win, I'm certain that there will be no lack of students knocking upon my door.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Moreover, research resources will be made available to the victor, so that will nix my funding issues. Therefore, my two juniors, I do apologize, but I fully intend to emerge triumphant.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I—I'll do my best as well. At least, I don't plan to lose too badly...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So why are you here, Layla?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I don't know why, but a lot of people recommended me. I didn't sign up myself. I just woke up to find my name on the announcement board.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounds like what happened to Tighnari!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Him too?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I'm... I'm really nervous. I've been so worried about disappointing everyone that I've been losing sleep...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Stress not, young one. We must all experience failure to grow and mature.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: But Madam Faruzan, I don't want to fail...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Tch, seriously? Everyone has such nice reasons for joining.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And what's your story, Kaveh?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Must I say?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes, you do! We gotta record it!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Um, well... You know, right? I want to buy some property...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, that's right! You want to move out of Alhaitham's—

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *coughing* What!? Alhaitham? What about him!? This has nothing to do with him!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon's misremembering things.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh...! Right! Sorry, Paimon has no idea what she was talking about...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, you want to use the grand prize to buy a place, right?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Correct. Also, my father took part in the Interdarshan Championship when I was young, but he didn't win.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Once I do, the right to wear that diadem will be mine. In a way, I'll be helping my father fulfill a dream of his.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: That's not a bad reason at all. You have ambition, youngster.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Although your chances with me here aren't great, I believe your father would be most proud if the Diadem of Knowledge were bestowed upon you.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Not that he'll have the chance to celebrate. My father passed away many years ago. They say he ran into quicksand while traveling in the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: For you to have experienced such a thing... That must have been tough for you.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: It's all in the past now, and life goes on, doesn't it? Let's change topics — I don't want to bring the mood down.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Alright. Earlier, you said that you want to use the prize Mora to purchase a home. Where do you live now, do you live alone?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *cough* Well...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Hmm... I also heard you mention "Alhaitham" just a moment ago. Isn't he also from Haravatat? Are you two hiding something from me?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: No, of course not! Why would you think that? Hahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's definitely not involved, either! We're gonna go interview other contestants now! Bye!

talks.objective: Ask the representatives their reasons for participation

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, so... what... what, uh...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Just call me Hat Guy. That's the name I use in Vahumana.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounds like a nickname, not a real name!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: So I can't go by a simple, ordinary name?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fine, suit yourself. Alright then, Hat Guy, why are you taking part in the Interdarshan Championship?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're specially invited guest commentators, so play nice and answer our questions.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You could be matra for all I care. So what if I don't answer you? What then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You...!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Hmph, I'll tell you this much: I have an agreement with someone not to reveal my motives.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're not plotting something in secret, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Well, it's hard to say. Why don't you take a guess?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon's had it with you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fine, be that way! Then we won't ask you why you're participating. Instead... Uh, why did you join Vahumana?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You two sure like to poke your noses where they don't belong. If I don't say anything, are you going to annoy me to death?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...I heard that the Vahumana researcher named Aqaba was researching the Tatarasuna incident, so I wrote a few essays to refute his points.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Later, when I was bored, I wrote some commentary on societal issues in Inazuma. I didn't expect Vahumana to consider me as one of them. Someone even invited me to a lecture or whatever.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: From start to finish, it was just the wishful thinking of idiots — a misunderstanding. There's your answer. Simple.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: But when Lesser Lord Kusanali heard about this, she went out of her way to get me registered in Vahumana... She used the name "Hat Guy."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So it was Nahida's doing...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Enough chit-chat. You're better off wasting your time with the other contestants.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Someone's about to get very unlucky — wanna guess who?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How is anyone supposed to relax with you around!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've gotta stay alert and keep a close eye on him!

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Ah, you must be the guest commentators Wiqas invited. I've heard about you.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: I saw you two having quite the lively conversation, so I thought it would be best to wait. Are you two free right now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We were actually looking for you, too!

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Excellent! Then, please allow me to explain your job responsibilities in detail.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: First, please take these two things.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: The first item is a custom Kamera from the Akademiya. Please use it to record the competition as it unfolds.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: The second is an event-specific locator that will flag all participants' locations. It will also sound when one of them completes an objective.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, what a convenient little thing!

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Aside from you two, there are two other commentators. However, they will remain by the commentators' area and will not be following the contestants in real time.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, you probably know them... Alhaitham and Nilou.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh, it's them! We have to go over and say hi later!

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Well, don't let me keep you, unless you have any questions for me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you seen a white-haired man around?

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Hm? Why do you ask?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I saw someone like that on the stage earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Really? I didn't see any such person. Could I ask when you saw him?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just before the Akademiya representatives went on stage.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Strange... I was on stage the entire time, and I didn't see anyone come up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon didn't see anyone, either!

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Hehe, perhaps you're mistaken. However, if you have any leads on that matter, you can talk to me at any time—

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}, Paimon! Long time no see!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dehya, Candace! You two are here as well!

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Ah, so they're two friends of yours? In that case, I'll take my leave. May you all have a wonderful time during the Extravaganza!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: The Akademiya sent us both invitations, so Dehya suggested that we come together.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: The villagers were also encouraging me to travel outside the village. I couldn't find it in myself to turn them down...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: We're here now, so no point dwelling on that. Even though this Extravaganza isn't a holiday or anything, it's still a big deal here in Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Merchants from all over will set up shop. There'll be tons of stuff to eat, use, and wear... More than you can count!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I'm already set on helping you buy two new outfits. I mean, who wears the same thing at work and home, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I'm looking forward to it. Ah... Just being able to relax and wander the streets freely has already made my day.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: #So, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, you two wanna come with?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Agh, we'd love to... but we've got work to do right now!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Aw, that's a shame. Let's hang out together when you're free, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: In that case, Candace and I will head out first. Good clothing and fabrics are very much in demand — if you snooze, you lose! Oh, right, we should also get some accessories...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: No need to rush. I think we'll have a better time if we take things slow.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: See you two later. Feel free to come find us whenever you have the time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon didn't think that Candace and Dehya would come. Hanging out with them sounds like a great time! Still, looks like the competition's starting soon. Let's go over to where Alhaitham is and see what's going on.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Layla! Hmm? You look a little worried.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Yeah... I have no idea what I should do. What color are these Swiftflies? Do they have special markings? How do they differ from ordinary butterflies?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I can't even figure out these basic questions, and most of what I've learned in the past is completely useless here...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Aren't people who research the stars supposed to have some extraordinary abilities? Why not use astrology to solve it?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Oh, you're another contestant... Hat Guy, was it?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Is it that you can't use astrology during the day? Huh, guess that skill's less useful than I thought.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: No, it's not like that. If it's daytime, all I need is an astrolabe...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So why don't you do that, then?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Mona Megistus the Astrologist said that those who constantly use astrology to obtain things that shouldn't be theirs will eventually lose the "blessing from the stars."

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Um, it's just something I read in an academic publication. I really love to read Mona's essays...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You're overthinking it. Power is just a tool. It just seems to me that you don't have the resolve to win this. Well, suit yourself. Wallow in your immature ideals if you like.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Seriously? Just walking off after saying a bunch of mean stuff like that?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Um, did I say something wrong just now?

choices.text: No, it's good to have your own convictions.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Thank you so much. I've made up my mind not to use astrology for this. I think I'll just try my luck in the city.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: To be honest, I've always been pretty good at observation, and if I'm fortunate, I might be able to find that special butterfly species...

response.speaker: Bahir
response.text: Lord Cyno seems to have found a Swiftfly! Come on, let's go check it out!

response.speaker: Alae
response.text: Really? Where?

response.speaker: Bahir
response.text: The butterfly flew up high, and he's chasing it now!

response.speaker: Alae
response.text: Oh, no time to lose! Let's go see!

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: As expected of Cyno... Ah, actually, shouldn't you two go have a look as well? The moment when he catches the butterfly will likely be one worth recording, after all.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: I'll head into the city shortly to start my own search. I'll see you later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright. In that case, let's go see Cyno first, and then we can check on what everyone else is up to!

choices.text: It was just a difference in perspectives, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We found you, Cyno— Oh, wait, is that a Swiftfly?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Stay put, don't move...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, he caught it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Cyno? What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: This isn't what I'm looking for. It's a—

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *huffing*... Finally, I made it. I heard that you caught a Swiftfly, Cyno. Mind letting me see what it looks like?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Hold on, isn't this the mechanical bait that I released earlier? Why would you catch that instead of a Swiftfly!?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Wait a minute. If we consider this from a different angle, isn't it a good thing that the bait you made was convincing enough to fool even Cyno?

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: That's right. During a previous interior design project, I felt that the artificial flowers on the wall were a little bland, so I decided on placing a few moving mechanical butterflies to add some pizazz.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: In order to make them both small and nimble, I consulted with Madam Faruzan.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Not long ago, the two of us took all those mechanical butterflies and released them into the city—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why would you do that?

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Hmph, need you even ask? Young people these days really do need to get out more.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Have you never played that game where you place strips of paper on a bamboo pole and wave it across a field of flowers to attract a whole kaleidoscope of butterflies?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: No, I haven't.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Wait. So you're trying to...

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: That's right. The butterflies within the city will mistake our mechanical bait for one of their own and follow them around.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: As long as we keep releasing and retrieving our bait, we can capture all the butterflies within the city. What comes afterward is just a matter of separating the Swiftflies from the others!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, guess that's one way to do it.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Do not underestimate the wisdom of your elders. I had already thought of this method the moment the round's rules were announced.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Of course, we also owe much to this fine junior of mine here for making such lifelike butterflies. It seems that Kshahrewar has not quite declined as far as I had thought in recent years — their teaching skills, at least, seem to be intact.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Well, I just stuck to what I do best. The idea was yours.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Ah, no need to be so polite. Once we capture all these butterflies, we shall split the points for this round...

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Ah, look, one of them is returning now... Hmm? Wait a moment. Are my eyes deceiving me? Why don't I see any butterflies behind it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's because there are none! Seems like your plan has hit a snag.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Looks like the match continues. I'll be looking elsewhere.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Hmm, strange... Has something else diverted their attention?

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Come! Let's search in the direction the bait returned from!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll go have a look, too!

talks.objective: Discover the truth as to why the butterflies are lingering

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Faruzan, Kaveh, why did you two stop?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Ah, so it was the Amurta boy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tighnari!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Fascinating, isn't it? The butterflies have all congregated here, due to a special incense that I used.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I infused it with three different types of honey, and the butterflies, following the fragrance, have gathered around me.

dialogues.speaker: Huwa
dialogues.text: Butterflies must have really sharp noses, then!

dialogues.speaker: Huwa
dialogues.text: Wait... Do they even have noses? I've never seen one.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: They do not, in fact, and their vision isn't stellar, either.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: However, they can use their antennae to distinguish between scents, and their olfactory senses are generally quite advanced, allowing them to detect floral fragrances from great distances.

dialogues.speaker: Huwa
dialogues.text: Oh, so that's how it is! I had a pet butterfly once. I picked wild flowers and placed them in its box, but it wouldn't eat any...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That's normal. Raising butterflies isn't difficult, but there are many things you should take note of.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Appropriate temperature, sufficient air, and a spacious environment are examples of such considerations. You must also ensure that the food you've chosen suits their "palate."

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Most importantly, you must curb your curiosity and avoid disturbing them while they rest, otherwise they may become stressed.

dialogues.speaker: Huwa
dialogues.text: Ah, sorry, I liked to poke at its wings at the time...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Humans tend to rear many creatures due to their aesthetic value, but not all are suited for such a process.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Caring for living beings is hard work. Impulse alone is insufficient — some prerequisite knowledge is always required.

dialogues.speaker: Haryadi
dialogues.text: You sure do know a lot!

dialogues.speaker: Habib
dialogues.text: I—I have a question, too. I bought a scarab not long ago, and it hasn't seemed very active. Can you help me figure out why?

dialogues.speaker: Aymar
dialogues.text: I'd like to keep a Dusk Bird as a pet. What are some key points I should consider?

dialogues.speaker: Mahar
dialogues.text: Um... Is it possible to keep a Rishboland Tiger as a pet?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Alright, it seems like you all have a great deal of questions.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: But I'm in the middle of the Interdarshan Championship at the moment, so I'm afraid I can't answer them all now.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Let me propose an alternative. Next month, there will be a biology lecture at Gandharva Ville, and I will be sharing some interesting insights on living organisms there.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: If you're interested, you can attend that lecture, and if you should have any questions, just prepare them ahead of time. I'll answer questions after I've finished speaking.

dialogues.speaker: Huwa
dialogues.text: Alright! I'll be there!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Of course, please try to ask more... rational questions. For example, whether you can raise a Rishboland Tiger as a pet or not is mainly dependent on whether you can overcome one in a fight.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like Tighnari's science lecture will draw quite a crowd!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh! Ahem, was I listening in for that long?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Seems Collei's master does live up to his title as a teacher...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Madam Faruzan, I've had a look around. Nearly all the butterflies in this area have been attracted by the incense.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: However, we can cast our bait further away to avoid this area.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Alright, then let's get moving. We shan't let all the butterflies get away from us if we can help it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like the competition's really heating up. Let's go see how the other contestants are doing!

talks.objective: Observe and record the circumstances of other competitors

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Layla! How are things going on your end?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I've been searching for quite a while now, but I haven't seen any sign of the Swiftflies yet.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Instead, I ended up catching a few mechanical devices that looked very similar to butterflies. I wonder where they came from...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like Faruzan and Kaveh's devices are everywhere now...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I'll keep up the search. That said, I've noticed that the number of butterflies in the city has already decreased a lot compared to when the event started.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Probably because the other contestants are coming up with their own ways to catch butterflies... Alright, I'll do my best, too. Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's this?

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Oh, what a coincidence. I guess I just need to catch it now, right?

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Oh, um, please wait! Ah, there it goes...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's so fast! Paimon thought Alhaitham said they were only a little faster!

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: No, come back!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #C'mon, {NICKNAME}! Let's go, too!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Oh, it just occurred to me that we should also get you a makeup box.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: No, it's fine. I don't think I'll end up using it.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Maybe you won't, but it doesn't hurt to have one, right?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: C'mon, just trust me on this one...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Huh? Who are you, and what do you want?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: P—Please... don't move...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: "Don't move"? Who sent you?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Dehya...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I can handle this. Now, tell me, what do you want?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I believe she's looking for this. Here, take it.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: A—A butterfly? Was it on my head?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Oh, you're—

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: It's been a while, Layla.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: A friend of yours? Oh, so she must be the one you were telling me about...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You two know each other?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah... it has been some time. The first time I ever woke up after sleepwalking, I somehow found myself in Aaru Village. Candace was the one who took care of me then.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: That's right. She didn't look well, so I gave her something to eat. She said a lot of complicated things about astrology, the night sky, the stars... Not sure I understood it all, but it sounded pretty enchanting.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Right, do you still want this butterfly? It seems like you were chasing it all the way here.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: It's of little use to me, but if you don't want it, I can release it.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Just let her have it. It's no big deal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Swiftfly was flying so fast, but you were able to catch it like it was nothing, Candace.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: It didn't seem that quick, really. I was actually worried that I would injure it, but I'm glad that didn't happen.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Anyway, sorry about the butterfly thing. With the way you suddenly came running over like that, I thought you were hired to take us out or something.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: On second thought, I guess I've never seen an assassin that looks tired with dark bags around their eyes... Oh, you must be taking part in the Championship? Take it from me, don't let it stop you from getting some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I'll do what I can. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: We'll be on our way, then. See you later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alrighty. Let's bring the Swiftfly back together with Layla!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It seems we have a third contestant who has returned with a Swiftfly.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: With that, the first round has come to an end. I anticipate that all of you will keep up the effort for the second round. Dismissed.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Ah, um... Your closing statement sounded so... How do I put it... Decisive?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, you could certainly stand to try being more decisive, Nilou. It would help you live more freely.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hang on a second! Who were the first two contestants with Swiftflies?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Tighnari was first, and as for the second... It's being discussed right now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's being discussed?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hey, Alhaitham, I think I've come up with a good idea.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Second place gets two points, right? Can't Madam Faruzan and I split the points between us?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Quite the imagination you have there. I've read the Championship handbook from cover to cover, and I never saw any rule which permits that.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Then we can just add a rule.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Do you really think I'd do that?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: C'mon, you're not going to stand in the way of my victory, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, you're free to send the organizing committee an application outlining your naive proposal. They'll get back to you within three working days.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Three working days? It'll be too late by then!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Unfortunately for you, even dreaming is gonna cost you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, Paimon gets it now. Kaveh and Faruzan found the second Swiftfly together, but the rules say that only one person can get the points...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Ah well, the rules are the rules. Since you call me "Madam" and politely asked for my help, I shall give you these points.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: So I'll put the points under Kaveh's name, then?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: No. If I take these points, won't that only detract from your contributions, Madam Faruzan?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You might be alright with that, but I cannot do it, not in good conscience.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I don't have any problem with it. There are two more rounds, after all. Losing one isn't a major setback.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: But if you insist, I have another method — we can draw lots to see who will receive the points.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: L—Lots, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: What? Is there something wrong with that idea?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...No. Let's do it.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll get the paper needed for the lots. Give me a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everybody watches Kaveh suffer a glorious and forthright defeat in the game of lots.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ugh, seriously...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, but it appears that luck was on my side this time.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: No, you do deserve it... I'm just lamenting my bad luck. Perhaps... *sigh* Perhaps that's why my life is rife with troubles...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Indeed, it's rare to see anyone with such terrible luck be so willing to decide victory via lots.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: And what would you know about that? I just...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: We can save bickering for later. Record the points under Faruzan, and that'll finally bring the first round to a close.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The second round will be held in the desert. We'll be moving our commentator's stand over to Aaru Village.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Let's meet up in Aaru Village once everything is ready. I'll announce the details of the second round then.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Till then, you have some free time. I'm off the clock at this point, so it's farewell for now.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Wait, Alhaitham! You...! *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Don't be upset, Kaveh. Sighing can carry away your good luck, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, so that's how it works? In that case, I'll take in some deep breaths. Maybe that'll help make up for all the luck I've lost!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *deep breath* It's really no big deal. Two points aren't enough to decide victory or defeat just yet.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I'll win the next round, you'll see!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Looks like you've managed to pick yourself back up, young man. Good. I must warn you, though, that I'm quite familiar with the desert. You'll have to try your best if you don't want to lose.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I'm no stranger to the desert either, I'll be fine. Alright then, that's enough chit-chat for now. I'm going to check the area out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... So the current standings are Tighnari in first place, Faruzan in second, and Layla in third.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess we should also take a nice break before the next round starts. But where should we go first?

dialogues.speaker: Morgiana
dialogues.text: Why, you two look a little lost. If you're not sure where to start enjoying the Akademiya Extravaganza, then may I suggest that you have a chat with our boss?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your boss? Who's that? Do we know them?

dialogues.speaker: Morgiana
dialogues.text: Hehe, well, only the most famous merchant in all of Sumeru — Lord Sangemah Bay!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean Dori!

dialogues.speaker: Morgiana
dialogues.text: Precisely! Our boss sent me to inform you two that she'll be waiting for you at Sumeru City's north gate.

talks.objective: Go to the suburbs and look for Dori

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: #Oho! Well, if it isn't {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Dori! Are you here to attend the Akademiya Extravaganza too?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Of course! People are practically flocking to Sumeru City. You couldn't ask for a better opportunity to do business!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: This is one of the entrances into the city, and it's very close to the Wisdom Gala booths. There'll be an endless stream of customers! Hehe, I can already hear the Mora going "clink-clink-clink" as they fill my coin pouch...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Well, is there anything you'd like to purchase? We've got everything you need and deals that can't be beat!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Well, do you have anything to eat?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Wait, we're celebrating the Extravaganza, and you're only thinking of eating— ahem, I mean, of cooourse we've got lots of things to eat! That said, I recommend that you also consider some of the great bargains we have going on.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: The Wisdom Gala is about to begin, and once it starts, each of the Darshans will prepare a small challenge for everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: And, just between us, I have some Super Booster Supplements for sale. Eat just one to boost both your strength and dexterity for a short time, allowing you to overcome any challenge!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No thanks, we'll pass. These little challenges are gonna be a cinch for the two of us, just you watch!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, Paimon just wants something to eat, please. If you don't have any food, then we'll go somewhere else.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, Mora is Mora, after all. What would you like to eat?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmmm... Well, Paimon's pretty hungry right now. Do you have any tahchin?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Let me see...

dialogues.speaker: Amur
dialogues.text: This is a huge job, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Ganjul
dialogues.text: If this works out, we'll be set...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Here you go! Two servings of tahchin! See? I told you there's nothing Lord Sangemah Bay can't procure!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yay! Uh... Huh? What are you looking at, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I thought I saw someone just now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? Who? Someone we know?

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Was it someone suspicious? Have we attracted some unwanted attention?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What's happening, Dori? Is there something else going on?

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: I don't know who you saw just now, but I do have some hard-to-come-by information about the Extravaganza. If you want to know more, we can talk business later.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Do you remember those things we made previously?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh? You mean...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: It's time for them to shine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks like Faruzan and Kaveh have some secret plan!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, hello there! Madam Faruzan and I are discussing how—

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Shh, hush now! The walls have ears around here. We should keep it a secret for now, though you'll find out what we have in store soon enough.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Come now, let's go — before the others act!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Alright, there's no time to lose. We're off to make our preparations. See you later!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hmm... This is basically what I'll need. Do you think you'll have any difficulties?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I have most of the reagents with me, and I can buy the rest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Collei, you're here too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, Tighnari, you have a master plan ready?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: My hypothesis is that the Swiftflies' morphological variations won't significantly affect their fundamental nature. So, I'm planning on using this to lure them out.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Of course, I could be wrong. Every mutation opens the door to new possibilities, especially when they are artificially introduced...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Details will have to wait until after the post-experimental analysis. For now, Collei and I are going to buy some reagents for our experiment. Alright, well, see you later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, see ya!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I will now announce the rules for the first round of the competition. Please listen carefully!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: During the opening ceremony, Akademiya staff released several cages of butterflies, and many of them are now fluttering within Sumeru City.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Amongst these butterflies, three of them will be special Swiftflies. They have a different appearance and also fly a little faster.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Your objective this round is to find a Swiftfly and bring it to me. Three points will be awarded to the first participant to return, two to the second, and one point to the third.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That is all for the first round. Should you require clarification on anything, please ask any of the other staff.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alhaitham's all business all the time, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm. That said, how did he get picked to be a commentator? Paimon's kinda curious...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Finding three specific butterflies in a place as large as Sumeru City sounds rather improbable...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: If these Swiftflies behave anything like regular butterflies...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'm off. It will take some time to search every corner of Sumeru City.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh? You're going, just like that?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: A champion walks the road to victory!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: My dear Kshahrewar junior, I have a plan. How about some cooperation between you and me?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Cooperation?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like everyone's got their own plans for this toughie.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're supposed to go on stage next, right? Uh, let's wait and see everyone's reactions first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait a minute, look! He seems to be observing the other contestants, just like we are!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We were right not to let our guard down!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hmm, the scent is starting to fade.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Seems the wind is stronger than I thought. The incense isn't going to last long...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: How could it not be real...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: What brings you two here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You're here having coffee? Aren't you supposed to be a contestant?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Is there really any need for me to take part while everyone's running around like it's some sort of carnival? Don't worry, I'll get involved once things actually get serious.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Let's wait here. Whew, seems my age is catching up with me.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Please lead the Swiftflies back here... I'm really counting on you.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Alae
dialogues.text: It's been a long time since the last Interdarshan Championship. How exciting!

dialogues.speaker: Aissa
dialogues.text: They say that Sachin was a Vahumana researcher and that he was a pretty famous genius. I guess geniuses always appreciate the knowledge of other geniuses, haha!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'm surprised you were willing to come to Sumeru City at all.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, the atmosphere at the Akademiya has improved immensely since Azar and his ilk were deposed. Master has been busy recently, so he hasn't had the time to instruct me or try to convince me to return to the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: So I've been occasionally visiting the city these days. Trade and business are in greater abundance here, so it's much easier to acquire necessary research equipment.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: You know, I was just thinking... How did the two of you meet?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I was wrestling with a particularly tricky problem, and she happened to pass by while I was puzzling over it at the House of Daena. She then proceeded to provide some comments.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: "Provide some comments"? I was bestowing instruction!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Hmph. In truth, I have no intention of solving Kshahrewar's problems for them, but I decided that this youngster seemed to have a decent attitude, and so we had a good chat.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: But ultimately, I am a Haravatat scholar, so please come to me with questions about linguistics next time.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Enjoy the Interdarshan Championship. This will be one to remember, I'm sure.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: The other contestants are all wearing tracking devices, so you can use your locator to find them more easily.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: This is my first time commentating for such a competition. I'm feeling kinda nervous.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nilou, how did you get picked to be a guest commentator?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: The staff said that spectators would be less inclined to come if the contestants and commentators were all from the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I don't quite understand it, but I'm happy that we're able to all meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I didn't expect that you would be invited as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Neither did we! Uh... by the way, how did you get picked, Alhaitham?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: There were several factors, but primarily the recommendation of the sages. I suppose they assumed that I'd have the free time for this job after resigning as Acting Grand Sage.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That said, they'd probably claim that my calm demeanor would help maintain fairness in the competition.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like you've got a lot on your plate...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Not really. The job itself is quite simple and effortless.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Let me find a good place to...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Are you sure it's alright to release so many?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Have some faith, it'll be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Good, we've got all our ingredients. Next, could I trouble you to help me mix them together?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Of course, Master!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I'm going to try my luck in the city, too.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Not here...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Wonder if I'll find one here.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: This is taking longer than I thought.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Whew... what a crowd. Seems the Akademiya Extravaganza is in full swing. What do you wanna get?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Hmm... Maybe we can buy some gifts to bring back?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Now? Huh... I usually get gifts last. Let's go walk around somewhere else first...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: These all look great, but they're more expensive than I expected.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Goods are more expensive here than in Aaru Village.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...Ah to heck with it! How often do you get to come to the city? Let's not get hung up over the prices!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Dehya, are you sure you want to buy this for me? ...Ooh, this is a heavier material than I expected. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it! It's just nice to go clothes shopping together.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like Kareena's got a moment now. Let's go chat with her!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The locator's going off!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like someone's already caught themselves a Swiftfly!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The locator's going off again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So someone else finished, too? That would mean that the one Layla's chasing is the last Swiftfly.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: (It doesn't seem that Sumeru City has changed too much.)

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: (I must get that limited-edition card!)

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: (With that prize money, I'll be able to move out of Alhaitham's place!)

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: (I'll show them how fierce this competition can be!)

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: (D—Do I really have what it takes to represent the Rtawahist Darshan?)

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: (Do you really think you can see through me?)

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: ("Face the Kamera, smile, speak in a friendly and clear manner"... That's what they told us to pay attention to, right?)

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: (I wonder who will emerge as the champion this time.)
